q: Alkyne molecules which are unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (C≡C) (____ bond).
e: Alkyne molecules which are unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (C≡C) (acetylenic bond). Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, so alkenes, alkynes and aromatics sit in that group. Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon triple bond and the general formula CnH2n-2. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

q: They form a homologous series, with the general formula ____, where n is a number equal to or greater than 2.
e: They form a homologous series, with the general formula C_nH2n-2, where n is a number equal to or greater than 2. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once. In a homologous-series formula, n is the number of carbon atoms in that member.

q: The representative alkyne given here is ____, $C_2H_2$.
e: The representative alkyne given here is ethyne, C_2H_2. Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon triple bond and the general formula CnH2n-2.

q: The first member of the series is known as ethyne, and it is commonly called ____.
e: The first member of the series is known as ethyne, and it is commonly called acetylene. The first member of the series is known as ethyne.

q: The suffix -ane of the alkane is replaced by ____.
e: The suffix -ane of the alkane is replaced by -yne. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2.

q: The chains with ____ or more carbon atoms lead to the formation of structural isomers in alkynes.
e: The chains with four or more carbon atoms lead to the formation of structural isomers in alkynes. Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon triple bond and the general formula CnH2n-2. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ.

q: ____ ($CaC_2$) reacts with water to produce acetylene.
e: Calcium carbide (CaC_2) reacts with water to produce acetylene. CaC_2 reacts with water to produce acetylene.

q: The calcium carbide required for this reaction is industrially prepared by heating calcium oxide with ____ in an electric furnace.
e: The calcium carbide required for this reaction is industrially prepared by heating calcium oxide with coke in an electric furnace. Carbide required for this reaction is industrially prepared.

q: At room temperature, alkynes containing two to four carbon atoms are gases; those containing five to twelve are liquids; containing more than thirteen carbon atoms are ____.
e: At room temperature, alkynes containing two to four carbon atoms are gases. those containing five to twelve are liquids. containing more than thirteen carbon atoms are solids.

q: Addition of water to ethyne yields vinyl alcohol which tautomerizes to ____ (acetaldehyde).
e: Addition of water to ethyne yields vinyl alcohol which tautomerizes to ethanal (acetaldehyde). An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon.

q: The order of the readiness with which the hydrogen halides add to ethyne is ____.

q: The addition reaction of vinyl bromide is in accordance with ____ rule.
e: The addition reaction of vinyl bromide is in accordance with Markownikoff's rule. In an addition reaction atoms add across a double or triple bond and unsaturation falls.

q: When acetylene is passed over heated sodium, one or both hydrogen atoms may be replaced or substituted by sodium to form mono- and di-sodium ____.
e: When acetylene is passed over heated sodium, one or both hydrogen atoms may be replaced or substituted by sodium to form mono- and di-sodium acetylides. One or both hydrogen atoms may be replaced or substituted by sodium to form mono- and di-sodium acetylides.

q: When ethyne is added to an ____ solution of copper(I) chloride or silver oxide, a precipitate is formed.
e: When ethyne is added to an ammoniacal solution of copper(I) chloride or silver oxide, a precipitate is formed. Listen for ammoniacal in that sentence.
